value.rationale: Centered geodesic-distance variance is a natural measure of dispersion in continuous transportation networks. The theorem gives a complete sharp optimum for every positive bridge length over all two-loop length allocations, identifies an unexpected unique symmetry-breaking region, and proves an exact threshold for loss of attainment. A contrasting strict mean-distance preference for equal loops within the same region shows this is not merely a restatement of known mean-distance formulas.
